justification: New state-law-only area check (low and mid-rise walking limit, Chapter 5 TOD map rule, s164 exclusions) built as pure rules plus live public map-service reads. It reads no database, writes nothing, and is not yet wired to any page or served number, so it is not Critical; it is more than Minor because a wrong answer here would later tell a person a lot is or is not in a reform area.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: Prints FAIL on the ALL line whenever the independent walking router's distance falls outside our stated range for more than 10 percent of lots, or any yes/no answer is opposite to the router, or real can't-tell exceeds 5 percent. Always-yes and always-no versions are scored in the same run and must also print FAIL.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: [ALL] lots 100: yes/no 79 (match router 75/79 = 95%, wrong-yes 0, wrong-no 0) | borderline 20 (lean matches router 14/20) | real can't-tell 1 (1%) / range validity: router's walk inside our range for 56/64 lots = 88% | median range width 300 m / => FAIL  (also: both fresh sets combined 103/120 = 86% before the range was made lopsided; always-yes matched the router on 42/100 and always-no on 38/100)
falsifiable_check.external_authority: The OpenStreetMap Valhalla pedestrian router is the judge. It is a different routing engine from our own footpath files and is never used by the check being tested. Both read OpenStreetMap, so a path missing from the map would fool both; that limit is stated in the report to the user.

pre_impl.existing_data: No database table is read or written. Reads are public NSW map layers (SEPP maps 752/759/776/766, EPI heritage 16 and State Heritage Register 221, bush fire prone land, council area, lot outline) and committed files: the saved SEPP Housing text facts (data/law/housing_sepp_lmr_facts.json), the station entrance file, and the packed walking files.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: If a map layer returns an unexpected shape or no answer, the value becomes None and the answer becomes cant_tell, never a clear. If a heritage class this code has not seen appears, the heritage answer is unknown. If a lot has no outline, no distance is computed. If a station is missing from the station file, no distances are computed.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Applies to every lot asked about at request time; nothing is stored per lot. The walking files cover five Sydney areas only; a lot outside them gets cant_tell with the reason 'no walking surface built for this area'.
pre_impl.external_source_error: A failed or empty public map call returns None (services/lmr_area_inputs.py _get_json), which layer_state reads as unknown. An ArcGIS error body without 'features' is treated as a failure, not as an empty result.
pre_impl.frontend_type: Not applicable: no frontend or API route is changed in this commit.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Not yet served to users. The answer carries clause, page and law version date; borderline lots show the walking range and the share of it under the limit; a failed measurement says cant_tell with the reason.

functions.name: decide
functions.input: dict of measurements (layer hits, council, distances, walk range) plus the saved law facts
functions.output: dict with pathway, headline, lmr answer, tod answer, not_checked list, notes
functions.if_none: any missing measurement gives cant_tell for that rule; a no from any rule is final; a yes needs every rule clear and the whole walking range under the limit; the function never raises

functions.name: walk_from_lot
functions.input: lot outline in metres, straight distance, packed walking surfaces, set of nearby anchors that must be built
functions.output: dict with walk metres, valid flag, reason, anchor, extra uncertainty for unmapped entrances
functions.if_none: no covering surface, thin network, no footpath within 40 m of the outline, a missing nearby anchor, or an impossible walk (shorter than the straight line) all give valid false with a reason, never a number

functions.name: gather
functions.input: latitude, longitude, optional lot outline, station file, walking surfaces, saved layer results
functions.output: measurement dict that is ready for decide
functions.if_none: no lot outline, unreadable station file or failed town centre map leaves distances None, so the answer is cant_tell

values.if_missing: constants; the printed explanation states the numbers and that they were measured on 248 lots against an independent router

values.name: heritage item class
values.value: LAY_CLASS from the EPI heritage layer
values.if_missing: an unknown class or a failed query makes the heritage answer unknown, which blocks a yes

queries.purpose: Which lot outline contains the address point (smallest containing polygon), with a fallback service
queries.where_clause: point intersects NSW Property layer 4, then NSW Cadastre layer 9; only a polygon that contains the point is kept
queries.if_zero: None, so no lot-outline rules or distances run and the answer is cant_tell
queries.if_wrong: a neighbouring polygon that does not contain the point is rejected by the contains test

queries.purpose: Is the address point or the lot outline on the TOD, accelerated TOD, exclusion or bush fire map
queries.where_clause: point query and polygon query against each ePlanning or BFPL layer, outFields OBJECTID only
queries.if_zero: a successful empty answer means clear; a failed call means None and unknown, never clear
queries.if_wrong: a lot only partly on a map is reported as part, not hit, and the decision does not treat part as clear

queries.purpose: Read the current Chapter 5 law figures for the TOD panel from the law_facts table
queries.where_clause: is_current AND instrument_key = 'sepp_housing_2021' AND fact_key = ANY(the five listed keys)
queries.if_zero: available true with no facts; the panel then prints a sentence with no figure
queries.if_wrong: a non-current or other-instrument row cannot be returned; a fact outside the list is never served

break_it.scenario: A lot near two anchors where only the farther anchor has a built walking file, so the shorter walk to the nearer anchor is never seen
break_it.what_happens: A wrong 'no' or a too-long walk would be shown with confidence
break_it.how: services/lmr_walk_surface.py:153 — every anchor within the straight-line limit must exist in a covering surface or the walk is invalid

break_it.scenario: A lot on a long street whose start point jumps sideways to a junction on another street because walking files only stored junctions (seen live on 2/87 Dunmore St South Bexley: walk 485 m against about 850 m)
break_it.what_happens: A wrong 'yes' that the independent router contradicts
break_it.how: services/lmr_walk_surface.py:42 and :175 — start reach cut to 40 m, snap slack 10 m, and the builder now stores a point about every 15 m along every street; the lot is now borderline with range 569-869 m and the router's 851 m falls inside it

break_it.scenario: The lot outline service returns a neighbouring or common-property polygon that does not contain the address point, or both outline services fail, so the smallest containing polygon is the wrong lot or missing
break_it.what_happens: Whole-lot rules and distances would be measured for the wrong parcel, or silently skipped
break_it.how: services/lmr_area_inputs.py:111 — only a valid polygon that contains the address point is kept, the smallest one wins, the Cadastre is the fallback service, and no outline means no distances and a cant_tell answer

break_it.scenario: A public map layer times out or returns an error body and the code reads it as 'not on the exclusion map'
break_it.what_happens: A lot on an excluded map would be told it is clear
break_it.how: services/lmr_area_inputs.py:70 — _get_json returns None unless the body has features and no error; layer_state turns None into unknown; a yes needs every rule clear

break_it.scenario: A heritage layer class the code has not seen, such as Local Heritage - General or an Aboriginal class, is treated as no heritage item
break_it.what_happens: A heritage-listed lot would be told it is clear for the low and mid-rise pathway
break_it.how: services/lmr_area_inputs.py:62 — item classes are listed explicitly, undecided classes and unknown classes give None, and only a successful query with no item class gives False

break_it.scenario: A station with no mapped entrance gets a guessed entrance that is presented as official
break_it.what_happens: A person reads an estimated point as a real public entrance
break_it.how: scripts/lmr_area/apply_entrance_rule.py — estimated entrances carry estimated true and 40 m extra uncertainty (measured: 96 percent of real entrances within 40 m); tests/test_lmr_data_files.py fails if an estimated entrance is unlabelled

break_it.scenario: The repo test setup replaces pyproj with a stub whose transform returns zero, so every distance is 0 and distance tests pass or fail for the wrong reason
break_it.what_happens: Projection tests would silently measure nothing
break_it.how: tests/lmr_gather_real_pyproj.py is not collected in a normal run and tests/test_lmr_area_inputs.py runs it in a child pytest with --noconftest; test_the_real_projection_is_in_use fails if the projection returns zero

break_it.scenario: The law figures for the TOD panel are typed into the page, so a change to section 155 never reaches the panel (the 22 m, 24 m and 2.5:1 sentence in StateLevelControls.tsx)
break_it.what_happens: The panel keeps showing an old figure after the law changes, with no test failing
break_it.how: frontend-nextjs/lib/law-facts.ts builds the sentence from the law_facts rows; frontend-nextjs/__tests__/lib/law-facts.test.ts changes a stored figure and requires the sentence to change, and fails if the component code contains a typed figure

break_it.scenario: The law_facts table is unreadable or empty when the TOD panel loads, and the page falls back to a default figure
break_it.what_happens: A made-up figure appears as if it were the law
break_it.how: frontend-nextjs/app/api/law-facts/route.ts returns 503 available false on a failed query; todStandardsSentence returns null when any of the three figures is missing and the panel prints TOD_STANDARDS_UNAVAILABLE, which contains no figure

break_it.scenario: The saved wording of s164(1)(g) is cut at a length cap, so only 17 of its 23 councils are known and a lot in one of the missing six is treated as outside the paragraph
break_it.what_happens: A flood-planning lot in Walcha or a neighbouring named council could be cleared by council name alone
break_it.how: scripts/extract_lmr_law_facts.py no longer caps the wording; tests/test_lmr_law_facts.py requires 23 names ending in Walcha and 6 lettered councils for (f1); the database row was corrected in place with scripts/load_law_facts.py --correct s164 and law_facts now equals the file

break_it.scenario: A lot in one of the 23 councils named in s164(1)(g) is answered yes because no flood answer was supplied to the area check
break_it.what_happens: A lot on a council flood planning map is told it is clear
break_it.how: services/lmr_area_decision.py — in a named council a missing, failed or non-boolean flood answer is unknown, which blocks a yes; services/lmr_area_inputs.py _flood_answer turns any failure into value None
break_it.repro: python -m pytest tests/test_lmr_area_decision.py -k g_applies_only; python -m pytest tests/test_lmr_area_inputs.py -k flood_function

break_it.scenario: The coastal vulnerability map is assumed empty because its label says 'No map at this time', but the layer holds 10 areas near Port Stephens and Coffs
break_it.what_happens: A lot inside one of those areas would be told it is clear
break_it.how: services/lmr_area_inputs.py queries layer 251 by lot outline like the other maps; a hit excludes, a part or a failed query blocks a yes; a point inside a real area hit on a live check 2026-11-07

break_it.scenario: The Python image copies only services/, so the law facts, station file and walking files are missing in production and every lot returns Not determined (or worse, a stale answer from a partial copy)
break_it.what_happens: The area check card shows Not determined for every address after deploy
break_it.how: Dockerfile.python now copies data/law/housing_sepp_lmr_facts.json, data/law/lmr_station_entrances.json and data/lmr_walk/; tests/test_lmr_data_files.py fails if any COPY line is removed

break_it.scenario: The area check service is slow, down or returns an error and the page turns that into a yes or a no for the lot
break_it.what_happens: A person is told a lot is or is not in a reform area when no measurement was made
break_it.how: frontend-nextjs/app/api/housing-sepp/area-check/route.ts returns 502 for any service error; hooks/useAreaCheck.ts lmrFlags maps borderline, undetermined and missing results to null; components/compliance/AreaCheckCard.tsx prints Not determined with a next step

break_it.scenario: The TOD parking card keeps typed distances (800 m rail, 600 m light rail, 400 m bus, 1,000 m search) that disagree with the law's accessible-area definition (800 m rail, light rail and ferry; 400 m bus)
break_it.what_happens: A lot is told parking reductions may apply or not apply on a figure the law does not contain
break_it.how: frontend-nextjs/lib/law-facts.ts accessibleAreaLimits reads the stored figures and returns null unless both exist; StateLevelControls.tsx makes no distance claim without them; the typed constants are deleted and frontend-nextjs/__tests__/lib/law-facts.test.ts fails if a distance-shaped 600 or 1000 or a *_M constant returns

break_it.scenario: The parking minimums are typed into the page, so a change to Chapter 6 never reaches it, or a section with no parking standard (s180) is shown with an invented rate
break_it.what_happens: The area card shows a parking rate the law does not contain
break_it.how: scripts/extract_lmr_law_facts.py _parking_minimums reads each parking sentence with its section and page; a section with no sentence yields no fact; frontend-nextjs/lib/law-facts.ts reformParkingRates labels each rate from the stored heading and types no figure; frontend-nextjs/__tests__/lib/law-facts.test.ts fails if 0.5, 0.4 or 0.2 appears in the code
break_it.repro: python -m pytest tests/test_lmr_law_facts.py -k parking; cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest __tests__/lib/law-facts.test.ts

break_it.scenario: A lot inside an airport noise contour band is told it is clear because the Sydney-only anef_zones table or a typed level is used instead of the law's levels and the portal's bands
break_it.what_happens: A lot at ANEF 25 or ANEC 20 or greater gets a yes, or (with the old table) about half of Sydney gets a wrong no
break_it.how: services/lmr_area_decision.py compares each band from planning portal layer 235 with the ANEF and ANEC levels read from the saved s164(1)(h) wording; a band that cannot be compared or a failed query blocks a yes; paragraph (h) stays listed as partly checked because Sydney Airport's own contours are not on the portal

break_it.scenario: A lot beside a gas pipeline is told nothing, or a lot far from the mapped lines is cleared of paragraph (i)
break_it.what_happens: A person assumes no pipeline was relevant
break_it.how: services/lmr_area_inputs.py queries Geoscience Australia's gas pipeline layer with the law's distance read from the saved facts; a hit is a warning that says whether it is a relevant pipeline was not checked; a miss or a failed call clears nothing and (i) stays in the not-checked list
break_it.repro: python -m pytest tests/test_lmr_area_decision.py -k pipeline; python -m pytest tests/test_lmr_area_inputs.py -k pipeline

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes: a person reads the printed Chapter 5 table and the lots listed as outside our range before any outreach; the outreach hold stays on
